function: Excluded (system): the learned SGP-LMC forecasts per-device SNR (channel prediction, area 2), but each link is single-antenna without RIS: scalar SNR g_i(t), r_i(t)=B log2(1+p_i(t)g_i(t)) (p. 4).
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match the PDF. Checks 1-5 pass: research article proposing a method; the learned component is a Gaussian-process forecaster (SGP-LMC) whose kernel parameters are trained by gradient algorithms, p. 8: "we invoke a light-weight learning technique, i.e., GP, for channel forecast"; it predicts the multi-slot-ahead SNR of each device, a channel prediction function (area 2), while offloading and power allocation use Lyapunov optimization (pp. 5-7), so the learning does not act above the PHY. Check 6 applies: the MEC uplink gives each device a designated channel with a scalar SNR, p. 4: "gi (t) represents the SNR from mobile device i to the MEC server" and "ri (t) = B log2 (1 + pi (t)gi (t))"; neither the system model nor Table I (p. 4) has antenna arrays, beamformers, or a RIS, and the simulation uses scalar fading, p. 10: "independent Rayleigh fading with distance-dependent path loss". IRS appears only as motivation in the abstract and related work (pp. 1-2). Single-antenna links without RIS in an area 2 work, so exclude for system; the simulation results (pp. 10-12) would otherwise satisfy check 7.
